short: Sensing, shared model and joint word-plus-identity output are each standard; whisper adds nothing over the 91.4% ultrasonic-only baseline, and impostors are training participants (M12 behind).
position: HEar-ID [@dong2025hearid] changes the sensing (in-ear ultrasound plus whisper, M05), the model (shared encoder with contrastive, triplet and CTC heads, M06), enrollment (M03) and the output (word plus accept or deny, M08). Each is standard: audio-plus-ultrasound fusion [@zhu2007multimodal], headphone echo sensing [@zhang2023hpspeech], verification from murmured speech [@okamoto2007nam] and content-plus-identity output [@chetty2008avfusion] predate it; what is new is the combination on one earbud. The whisper stream shows no gain: on the 8 of 11 users without degraded ultrasonic sensing, Top-1 is 90.25% against 91.4% for the authors' ultrasonic-only ReHEarSSE pipeline [@dong2024rehearsse], and 67.3% over all users (§4.1.2). Authentication is tested only against the other participants, whose data also train the model (§4.1.1), so M12 is behind; replay, the attack that motivates the paper (§1), is never tried.
